did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with a call to sing to the Lord a “new song”—a song fitting for the wonderful deed and salvation the Lord accomplished by his power, described through his “right hand” and “holy arm.”
Did you know? The Lord’s salvation is not presented as a hidden event: the Lord makes his salvation known and reveals his righteousness in the sight of the nations.

Did you know? The psalm connects the Lord’s steadfast love and faithfulness toward the house of Israel with making his salvation known to “all the ends of the earth”—in other words, the message expands from Israel to the whole world.
Did you know? The call to praise is addressed to “all the earth” and includes three expressions of joyful sound: shouting, bursting into song, and singing praise.
Did you know? The psalm mentions the lyre as an instrument accompanying the singing, and the phrase “with the sound of singing” emphasizes that the music joins the human voice.

Did you know? Alongside the lyre, trumpets and the ram’s horn are mentioned; they sound before the Lord, who is described here as “the King”—a picture of welcoming his reign with joy and loud acclaim.
Did you know? The singing in the psalm is not limited to human beings: the sea, all that fills it, the world, and its inhabitants are portrayed as shouting and joining in response to the Lord.
Did you know? This verse personifies nature: the rivers are described as clapping their hands and the mountains as singing together for joy.
Did you know? The climax of the psalm is the Lord’s coming to judge the earth; the judgment is described as his judging the world and the nations with righteousness, fairness, and uprightness.
